statement: For iid Rademacher R in dimension n>=2 and v=(1,-1,0,...,0)/sqrt(2), P(<R,v>=0)=1/2, refuting an all-deterministic-unit-vector bound P(|<R,v>|<=t)<=Kt at t=0.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently enumerated (++),(+-),(-+),(--): two equal-sign cases give zero. Norm of v is 1.
remaining_gap: Only refutes an overly uniform row small-ball bound; random-normal structure remains unproved.

statement: The C0029-A001 assertion that the finite-n real Gaussian least-singular-value CDF equals 1-exp(-t^2/2-t) is false; this expression is a limit law, not the finite-n exact CDF.
assumptions: At n=1, G=[Z] with Z standard normal, and t=1.
source_quote: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t)
proof_or_counterexample: For n=1, P(|Z|<=1)=erf(1/sqrt(2))=0.6826894921370857 whereas 1-exp(-3/2)=0.7768698398515702. Reproduction: python -X utf8 -c with math.erf and math.exp, values recorded in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: Replace the archive statement through a separate authorized correction process; this correction does not resolve C0029.

statement: For an (n-1)-by-n real D and appended row X, the threshold event s_min([D;X^T])<=r is automatic if s_min(D)<=r, and otherwise is equivalent to |<v,X>|^2 <= r^2(1+sum_i <v_i,X>^2/(s_i^2-r^2)).
assumptions: n>=2, r>=0, D full row rank with s_min(D)>r on the second branch; singular vectors as in w564 ATTEMPT.md.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently rederived from congruence of AA^T-r^2I with positive DD^T-r^2I and its scalar Schur complement; interlacing handles d<=r, including equality and rank deficiency.
remaining_gap: Exact deterministic equivalence supplies no probabilistic sharp bound.

statement: The Rademacher-minus-Gaussian CDF difference equals the sum over k of the averaged conditional row-probability differences for mixed skeletons D_k; each difference vanishes when s_min(D_k)<=r.
assumptions: Independent rows and entries in A_k; first k Gaussian rows, remaining sign rows; r=epsilon/sqrt(n).
proof_or_counterexample: For each k, condition on the same independent skeleton D_k; p_{k-1}-p_k=E(Q_R-Q_G). Sum over k=1..n and cancel intermediate p_k. On d<=r both Q terms equal 1.
remaining_gap: Need a signed estimate on the entire averaged sum; no pointwise sign is available.

statement: For a Sylvester Hadamard skeleton D at n=2^m and r=1/[8(n+1)], Q_R(D,r)-Q_G(D,r)>=3/[4(n+1)].
assumptions: n=2^m>=2; D is H_n with the all-ones row removed; appended row has iid signs or standard Gaussians.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently checked D^TD=nI-nvv^T and the two-dimensional block of A^TA has trace 2n, determinant S^2; its minimum eigenvalue is n-sqrt(n^2-S^2). Nonzero S yields eigenvalue at least 2/n>r^2, while P(S=0)=binom(n,n/2)/2^n>=1/(n+1). Gaussian normal projection is independent of tangent squared norm W~chi-square(n-1); density bound and Jensen give Q_G<=2r=1/[4(n+1)]. Reproduction table n=2,4,8,16 in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: Structured skeleton is rare in iid ensemble; no implication that the parent bound fails.

statement: The signed mixed-row estimate H of w564 is equivalent to the coefficient-one parent bound on 0<=epsilon<1, using exact L2 and trivial epsilon>=1 cases.
assumptions: As in L2, F_n is the all-Gaussian CDF, and q in (0,1) is absolute.
proof_or_counterexample: Algebraic equivalence follows from p_R=F_n+sum; the inequality itself has no proof.
remaining_gap: Prove H with its full signed averaged estimate; this is the hardest open piece of this route.
verdict: KEEP as open reduction, not as proof

statement: If n is even and D has n-1 iid uniform sign rows of length n, P(the rows of D are pairwise orthogonal) <= [2^-n binom(n,n/2)]^(n-2) <= 2^-(n-2). For n>=4, a mixed skeleton with an independent Gaussian row has probability zero of exact pairwise orthogonality.
assumptions: Even n>=2; independent iid signs for all-sign case; at least one independent continuous Gaussian row for mixed case; n>=4 for mixed assertion.
proof_or_counterexample: Condition on first sign row. Each other row independently has zero dot product with it with probability p_n; pairwise orthogonality is a subset of their intersection. p_2=1/2 and p_(2m+2)/p_(2m)=(2m+1)/(2m+2)<1. A Gaussian inner product with an independent nonzero row equals zero with probability zero.
independent_reviewer: w569 requested in review packet; pending
remaining_gap: Only the exact orthogonal-skeleton family is charged; near-Hadamard and other arithmetic skeletons remain, and H is unproved.

statement: In the H_4 skeleton with last row removed, t=3/4 and an iid sign appended row, the true dependent-radius event has probability 7/8, whereas independently resampling the row inside its radius gives 13/16.
assumptions: Fixed 3-by-4 Sylvester Hadamard skeleton; independent uniform sign row; t=3/4.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently reproduced z^2 law: masses 6/16,8/16,2/16 at 0,1,4. Radius squared 9(119-16z^2)/880 admits z^2=0,1, so 14/16. Independent copy gives 6/16+(8/16)(14/16)=13/16.
remaining_gap: Shows only dependence substitution failure; epsilon=t*sqrt(4)=3/2 outside the hard target range.

statement: An abstract upper bound F_n(x)<= (1+(log n)^(-1/16))x does not imply F_n(x)<=x+C exp(-c n) uniformly x>=0 for any fixed C,c>0.
assumptions: n sufficiently large; abstract CDF F_n(x)=min(1,(1+delta_n)x), delta_n=(log n)^(-1/16).
proof_or_counterexample: F_n is the CDF of Uniform[0,1/(1+delta_n)]. At x_n=exp(-sqrt(n)), excess delta_n*x_n has logarithm -sqrt(n)-(1/16)log log n, whose ratio to n tends to 0, so it exceeds every C exp(-c n) eventually.
remaining_gap: Logical counterexample only; not a Bernoulli-matrix distribution.
